newsitem.title: USA: Oxford CEO sees savings from new system.
newsitem.headline: Oxford CEO sees savings from new system.

text.p: Oxford Health Plans Inc expects to save up to 20 percent per case from its new specialty care team approach to health care delivery, the company said Tuesday.
"The specialty case management can lower cost by up to 20 percent per case, on average," said Stephen Wiggins, chief executive officer of Oxford in an interview with Reuters.

Earlier, Oxford gave a presentation on its new approach to healthcare, which includes patients selecting care from teams of providers who bid for the business. The teams consist of physicians, hospitals and other health care providers.
"We would like to target 90 percent of our payments to these case packages," Wiggins said, noting that 75 percent of company payments go to specialist care.
Wiggins said the company already has about 200 different physicians bidding for different types of cases, such as hip replacement, or cataract surgery.

The old specialist system centers on the primary care physician serving as a "gatekeeper" to each of the various specialists involved in a case, such as an orthopedist and a radiologist involved in a hip problem.
According to a company spokeswoman, Oxford has already treated 50 patients, representing 24 types of cases, under the new approach since the beginning of 1997, when it was begun.
Wiggins said that the company expects to have bids on 75 types of cases by year end and 150 types of cases by the end of 1998.
